tour.name: King's Highway Private Tour from Amman to Petra: Madaba, Mount Nebo, Kerak & Shobak Castles
tour.subtitle: One of the oldest roads in the world, in a private day with a licensed guide and vehicle: the mosaics of Madaba and Mount Nebo, the dramatic Wadi Mujib canyon, the Crusader castles of Kerak and Shobak, and the Dana viewpoint, ending in Petra.

The Dana viewpoint over the Great Rift
Shobak Castle, Montreal of the Crusaders
tour.overview:
The King's Highway, mentioned in the Bible, has linked Egypt and Mesopotamia for thousands of years, running along the highlands east of the Dead Sea. Traders, Nabataeans, Romans, pilgrims and Crusaders all followed it. Today it is the most scenic route from Amman to Petra, crossing deep canyons and passing the great castles built by the Crusaders in the 12th century.

This private day takes you along it with a licensed guide and a vehicle, ending at your hotel in Petra.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start: your hotel in Amman
• End: your hotel in Petra (Wadi Musa)
• Type: private one-way tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Madaba.
• Mount Nebo.
• Wadi Mujib canyon.
• Kerak Castle.
• Dana viewpoint.
• Shobak Castle.

WHY THIS WORKS
The scenic route takes longer than the Desert Highway; a private vehicle makes it a rich day of sightseeing on the way to Petra.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, photographers and travellers heading to Petra.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you are short of time, take the Desert Highway, about 3 hours.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The road through Wadi Mujib winds steeply down and up. Bring layers; the highlands are cool.

days.name: Madaba, Mount Nebo, Wadi Mujib, Kerak, Dana and Shobak to Petra
days.description:
What to expect: the castles and canyons of the King’s Highway, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrances and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:00. In Madaba you see the Byzantine mosaic map of the Holy Land, and on Mount Nebo the Memorial Church of Moses and the view over the Jordan Valley.

The highway then drops into Wadi Mujib, a canyon more than a kilometre deep, with a viewpoint over the dam and the gorge, and climbs out again to Kerak. Kerak Castle, built from 1142, is a maze of vaulted halls, stables and tunnels on a ridge; your guide tells its story, including the Crusader lord Raynald of Châtillon and its siege by Saladin. You have lunch in Kerak.

Further south, you stop at the Dana viewpoint, where the land falls away into the Great Rift Valley above the stone village of Dana, and visit Shobak Castle, founded in 1115 by King Baldwin I as Montreal, standing alone on a hill. You arrive in Wadi Musa, near Petra, at about 17:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up in Amman.
08:45 – Madaba.
10:00 – Mount Nebo.
11:15 – Wadi Mujib canyon.
12:15 – Kerak Castle.
13:30 – Lunch.
15:00 – Dana viewpoint.
15:45 – Shobak Castle.
17:00 – Arrival at your hotel in Petra.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Combine with our Petra and Wadi Rum days.
• Bring a torch for the dark passages of Kerak.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is this tour one-way?
faq.answer: Yes, from Amman to Petra. A return version can be arranged.

faq.question: Can we bring our luggage?
faq.answer: Yes, it travels with you in the vehicle.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love exploring the castles.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The castles have uneven floors and stairs.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About 5 hours of driving with stops along the way.

faq.question: Can we stay in Dana?
faq.answer: Yes, a night in Dana with a hike can be added.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and layers; the highlands are cool.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Jordan: guides and drivers appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
